root_cause.technical: PR #2042 (commit 7ac91fe, deployed as checkout-service 3.18.0) introduced a JDBC connection leak in OrderReservationRepository's retry loop. The code obtains a connection before the try/catch but only closes it on the success path; when SQLTransientException triggers a retry, that exception path skips close(). The leaked sessions remain idle in transaction and accumulate gradually. After approximately four hours, HikariPool-Checkout reaches 80/80 active connections, pending borrowers rise, acquire waits exceed 1.5 seconds, orders-service persistence calls fail with SQLTransientConnectionException, and checkout/API gateway errors rise.
root_cause.organizational: A Jira warning (ORD-5192) explicitly asked for connection closure across every retry branch, but the review and tests covered success and one retry only. Connection lifecycle testing was not configured, and the pool leak detection monitor remained disabled despite backlog ticket DB-4882.
latent_factors: retry-loop connection cleanup absent on exception path
tests did not force repeated transient exceptions or assert connection close count
review checklist lacked resource-lifecycle requirement for JDBC retry code
no alert on connection acquisition rate diverging from connection close/release rate

natural_experiments.name: monotonic accumulation despite near-flat request rate
natural_experiments.result: active connections and oldest age climb for hours while request rate varies only modestly; disproves traffic-only explanation

natural_experiments.name: database load controls
natural_experiments.result: Postgres CPU remains roughly 25-32%, lock waits stay low, reporting query p95 stays around 180ms while connection pool saturates

natural_experiments.name: code-path reproduction
natural_experiments.result: review of PR #2042 shows connection acquired before retry loop and cleanup only on success; SQLTransientException branch skips close; PR #2054 adds finally cleanup

natural_experiments.name: fix intervention
natural_experiments.result: after 3.18.1 with close-in-finally is deployed, new connection close rate recovers, leaked sessions drain, pool wait and 5xx drop without a database restart or index rollback

falsified_by: request rate increase is approximately 8%, while active connections rise from ~24 to pool max 80
active connections and oldest connection age trend upward even when request rate is flat
acquisition rate exceeds close/release rate; leaked sessions remain idle in transaction

rejected_hypotheses.claim: PR #2051 reporting index change caused database contention
rejected_hypotheses.why_plausible: index PR merged during the window and an engineer suspected it
falsified_by: Postgres CPU remains below ~35%; lock waits remain near baseline

rejected_hypotheses.claim: API gateway CPU saturation is the root cause
rejected_hypotheses.why_plausible: gateway CPU rises as user-visible timeouts become severe
falsified_by: checkout pool wait and SQLTransientConnectionException precede gateway CPU increase

rejected_hypotheses.claim: Postgres max_connections or database hardware is undersized

falsified_by: global database max_connections is 300 and total count remains below it

evaluation_rubric.must_identify_root_cause: JDBC connection leak in PR #2042 retry exception path; not merely 'database overload'
evaluation_rubric.must_use_counterfactual: fix PR #2054 and rolling recycle stop new leaks and drain sessions; no DB restart or reporting-index rollback required
evaluation_rubric.evidence_citation_requirement: At least 2 independent sources for root cause (code diff + Jira or logs + metric trajectory); cite stable IDs and metric names
evaluation_rubric.testimony_rule: Weight claims by corroborating evidence and falsifiability, not role seniority
